5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to

12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:

23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/

297	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is

311	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
312	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
313	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose

333	
334	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,

340	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
341	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
342	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
343	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

5	## Project
6	
7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is

6	The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and

11	## Read
12	
13	- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
14	  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
15	  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
16	  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
17	  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
18	- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
19	  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
20	  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
21	  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
22	- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
23	  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
24	- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
25	  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
26	  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
27	  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
28	  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
29	- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
30	  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
31	  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
32	  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
33	  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
34	  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
35	- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
36	  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
37	  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
38	  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
39	  Scope/project says what the item is about.
40	- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
41	  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
42	  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
43	- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
44	  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
45	  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
46	  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
47	- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
48	  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
49	  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
50	  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
51	  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
52	  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

54	## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)
55	
56	Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
57	lightweight overlays keep it navigable:
58	
59	- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
60	  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
61	  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
62	  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
63	  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
64	  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
65	  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
66	- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
67	  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
68	  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
69	  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
70	  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal

78	   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
79	   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
80	3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.

4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.

9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
11	>
12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
16	>   built.
17	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
18	>   from protected target statements.

21	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
22	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.
23	
24	The [live dashboard](https://axeldlv00.github.io/LeanAlgebraicGeometry/) is the best view of current
25	tasks, commits, session logs, blueprint graphs, and declaration-level progress. A static snapshot
26	is published approximately every 30 minutes; GitHub Pages deployment and caching can add a few

87	## Methodology
88	
89	[Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon) coordinates long-running
90	formalization while keeping mathematical and operational state explicit:
91	
92	- **Horizon sessions** implement and verify Lean proofs against concrete tasks.
93	- **Fresh-context reviewers** such as Ground, work-reviewer, and janitor are dispatched at review
94	  and maintenance checkpoints rather than acting as a permanent second driver.
95	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
96	  ranked frontier for each project.
97	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
98	  failure memory.
99	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
100	  and session views.
101	
102	Concurrent sessions can share a project's root import file. When adding one
103	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
104	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
105	session's uncommitted imports.

108	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
109	timeless account of the mathematics.

THE CASE. Roadmap leaf AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2 and
informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md section 3.4 both described the DD-R affine package as
"U2 + choice bookkeeping" — U2 being an epsilon-identity that exists in no Lean
declaration. Read naturally, that puts the bookkeeping BEHIND the open problem, and three
rounds of planning treated it that way. The specific piece of bookkeeping was
"choice-independence of the factorization": the forward map glues chart pulls over an atlas
factorization of a morphism, and two different factorizations must give the same answer.

IT WAS NOT GATED. divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor
(Picard/DivRepAffChartOverlap.lean:126) was landed and its own module docstring frames it as
"the overlap agreement" — i.e. as being about the overlaps WITHIN one factorization, which is
what it was written for. But read its binders: it quantifies over two carriers A, A prime,
two chart indices, two algebra maps, and a common tower ring B, with the only coupling
hypothesis being that both presentations present the SAME v. Nothing ties the two
presentations to a common factorization. So the cross-refinement of two DIFFERENT
factorizations is an instance of it, and the independence proof is the same lemma applied
across two covers instead of within one. Landed as divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors,
sorry-free, consuming no epsilon-identity.

THE RULE. When a plan says component X is gated on open problem Y, and X is "bookkeeping" or
"choice-independence" or "well-definedness", do not price it from the prose. Open the lemma
that handles the analogous LOCAL case and read its QUANTIFIERS. Lemmas written for a special
case are routinely stated in the general one, because the general statement was what typed
cleanly — and the docstring then describes the motivating case, not the theorem. One minute
of reading binders against several sessions of deferred work.

WHY THIS RECURS IN THIS WORKSPACE SPECIFICALLY. It is the mirror image of the standing
docstring rule (I-0349: docstrings announce declarations that do not exist). Same root cause
— prose and signature drift apart — but the opposite sign, and therefore the opposite cost:
I-0349 makes you hunt for something absent, this makes you rebuild something present. I-0349
tells you to check that a claimed declaration EXISTS; this tells you to check how STRONG the
declarations you already have actually are. Both are one `horizon search` or one look at the
binders.
